title: Fragrances For When Mariah Carey Is Getting a Little Too Carey’d Away
summary: Our Perfume of the Month is Moroccanoil L'Originale, paired with Drift Open Road as Cologne of the Month. Here's why we picked them.
body_markdown:
People have been begging Moroccanoil to turn its iconic haircare scent into a perfume for years. Well, you asked, they delivered, and now we’re delivering it straight to your door and pulse points.


We chose[Moroccanoil L’Originale](https://www.scentbird.com/perfume/moroccanoil-l-originale-99233358599502) as our Perfume of the Month for a very good reason. When everything smells like eggnog, cinnamon, and gingerbread, the color palette is red/green/gold, and every shop window competes to out-twinkle the next, our senses work overtime. And they are subtly asking for a vacation. In my case, sometimes the ask is not subtle at all. The senses yearn for places, preferably warm, with a sea breeze and absolutely no Christmas carols on repeat.


And L’Originale is the golden ticket to those faraway places.


Opening with sweet violet, blooming camellia, and a soft splash of citrus, L’Originale brings lots of sunshine to the shortest days of the year. At its heart, lily of the valley meets velvety woods and sheer vanilla before settling into the creamy warmth of white sandalwood, musk, and spicy amber. This is a fragrance moonlighting like a change of scenery for your senses, balancing airy florals with comforting warmth and just enough sweetness to make you forget about the freezing temperatures outside.


Of course, L’Originale is perfectly lovely on its own. But if you insist on layering (and we know some of you will), here’s a little insider tip: this perfume gets along especially well with fruity notes. We’ll let you choose which one to pick (pun very much intended).


When yours truly was younger, I was a devoted fan of a British boy band sensation called Take That. And when the band’s lead singer and principal songwriter released his own debut solo album, Open Road, in 1997, I played that CD within an inch of its life. Sometimes all day, sometimes all night, usually because I’d fallen asleep before remembering to turn off the CD player.


Nearly three decades later,[Drift’s Open Road](https://drift.co/products/open-road?srsltid=AYCX9vIwNhyUgZ9VfT7LSDA7NrcqwlFR5anO-gKE1etQp9htrc_CSxal) has brought back that same slightly obsessive feeling. Only instead of hitting replay, I keep bringing my wrist to my nose for another sniff. And another. And another. And another. And, well, you get the picture.


Which is precisely why we’ve chosen Drift Open Road as our Cologne of the Month.


This fragrance feels and smells wonderfully liberating. Bergamot sets the pace with a bright, exhilarating burst of citrus, while black pepper and elemi introduce a lively, aromatic spiciness that keeps things interesting. As the freshness settles, rich tonka and cedarwood take over, lending warmth, depth, and a smooth, woody finish that makes you want to revisit the whole experience from the beginning. A lot like me and that CD.


The holiday season has a funny way of making the walls close in. The calendar is packed, so are the shopping malls, and the four walls you’ve spent entirely too much time in feel restricting; so the appeal of an open road becomes almost irresistible.


An open road that leads to an open mind. To give this album a chance.


Speaking of music, I think it’s time to give that Gary Barlow album another spin.


## Frequently asked questions


### What is Moroccanoil’s Perfume of the Month?


Moroccanoil L’Originale, a floral fragrance based on the brand’s iconic haircare scent. It opens with sweet violet, camellia, and citrus, moves into lily of the valley and velvety woods, and settles into white sandalwood, musk, and spicy amber.


### What is Drift Open Road, and who makes it?


Open Road is one of Scentbird’s own owned fragrances under its Drift brand. It opens with bergamot, moves into black pepper and elemi, and finishes with tonka and cedarwood for a warm, woody-aromatic profile.


### Does Moroccanoil L’Originale perfume smell like the haircare line?


It’s inspired by Moroccanoil’s signature haircare scent but built out as a full fragrance, adding floral and woody layers like camellia, lily of the valley, and sandalwood around that familiar base.


### What does Drift Open Road pair well with for layering?


Its bergamot and spice-forward profile works well layered with other woody or citrus-forward fragrances, though it’s also designed to stand on its own.


### How can I try these fragrances before committing to a full bottle?


Both are available as 8 mL vials through Scentbird’s monthly subscription, giving you enough time to wear each one and see how it develops before deciding on a full-size bottle.
